system_overview: A refined specification of the resource allocator that adds a scheduling mechanism to prevent deadlocks. The simple allocator can paint itself into a corner by allocating resources in an order that prevents any client from obtaining its full request. This scheduling allocator maintains an ordered schedule of clients with outstanding requests and allocates resources respecting that order, ensuring that prioritized clients can eventually obtain all their requested resources.
actors_and_components: Three kinds of actors: client processes that request and return resources, the resource allocator that grants resources according to the schedule, and a scheduler component that determines the order in which clients with pending requests are served.
state_variables: Three state variables: (1) a mapping from clients to their sets of outstanding resource requests, (2) a mapping from clients to their sets of currently allocated resources, and (3) a sequence of clients representing the current schedule order. The schedule determines allocation priority.
initial_state: No resources have been requested or allocated, and the schedule is empty.
actions: Four actions exist. (1) A client requests a non-empty set of resources when it has no pending requests and holds nothing. (2) The allocator grants available resources to a scheduled client, provided no earlier-scheduled client has requested any of those resources; if the grant fully satisfies the client's request, the client is removed from the schedule. (3) A client returns a non-empty subset of held resources. (4) The scheduler appends clients with unsatisfied requests (not yet in the schedule) to the schedule in an arbitrary permutation order.
safety_properties: Resource mutual exclusion: no resource is simultaneously allocated to two different clients. A type correctness invariant constrains all state variables to proper types. A lower-level allocator invariant ensures: all scheduled clients have outstanding requests, no client holds resources requested by an earlier-scheduled client, and each scheduled client's request can be satisfied from currently available resources plus resources held by higher-priority clients.
liveness_properties: Three liveness properties hold: (1) clients will eventually return resources once their requests are fully satisfied, (2) every requested resource will eventually be allocated, and (3) each client's outstanding request set is infinitely often empty. Fairness conditions include weak fairness on returns (after request satisfaction), weak fairness on allocation, and weak fairness on scheduling.
model_bounds: For model checking: 3 clients and 2 resources. Symmetry reduction applies only to resources (not clients, because the schedule sequence breaks client symmetry).
additional_assumptions: The set of resources is assumed finite. The scheduling strategy is nondeterministic: clients are added to the schedule in any permutation order. This generality allows verification that correctness holds regardless of scheduling policy. The specification uses helper operators for computing permutation sequences of finite sets, removing elements from sequences, and computing the range of functions.
